personal.name: Yueqin Yin
personal.title: LLM Post-Training · Agentic RL · Data Synthesis · Alignment
personal.affiliation: The University of Texas at Austin, TX, USA
bio: I am a final-year Ph.D. student at the McCombs School of Business, The University of Texas at Austin, advised by Prof. Mingyuan Zhou, and will graduate in May 2027. My research focuses on LLM post-training, and my interests span:

(1) Agentic RL: long-horizon RL training for terminal and SWE agents (current focus)
(2) Data synthesis: verifiable training data for code and agents (KodCode; terminal and SWE agent datasets)
(3) Feedback and reward design: richer preference signals, better-targeted rewards, and grounded supervision (RPO, SAPO, Segment-PPO, MulIF, ContextCheck, SQL Autocomplete)
📢 I am on the job market! I am looking for full-time industry research scientist positions starting in 2027. Feel free to reach out!

research.description: I work on LLM post-training, with a focus on designing feedback a model can learn from: building more informative preference signals, directing rewards and exploration to the behaviors that still need work, and grounding feedback in execution and evidence, including in a deployed SQL autocomplete model that learns both what to suggest and when to stay silent. I am currently building training data for terminal and SWE agents and working on long-horizon RL.

news.content: Our paper on context-grounded data curation and gate-first RL rewards for SQL autocomplete {{link}}, from my Snowflake internship, was accepted to [[NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Transitioning from Pre-Training to Post-Training]].

MulIF {{link}} was accepted to [[EMNLP 2026 Findings]]. RL for multi-instruction following tends to over-optimize easy instructions; we correct this with behavioral bootstrapping and scarcity-aware rewards.
Joined Snowflake AI Research in Bellevue, WA as a research intern, working on code LLM post-training.
KodCode {{link}} received the Best Paper Award at the [[DataWorld Workshop @ ICML 2025]].

2022.title: TransEditor: Transformer-Based Dual-Space GAN for Highly Controllable Facial Editing
2022.tldr: A Transformer-based dual-space GAN that lets two latent spaces interact through a cross-space interaction mechanism, so the structure (e.g., pose) and texture (e.g., style) of a face can be edited independently. Improves controllability and identity preservation on CelebA-HQ and FFHQ.

2022.title: DiffGAR: Model-Agnostic Restoration from Generative Artifacts Using Image-to-Image Diffusion Models
2022.tldr: Introduces generative artifact restoration: removing the artifacts that GANs and diffusion models leave in their outputs. DiffGAR is a model-agnostic image-to-image diffusion framework for this task, released with two new datasets.

2023.title: Efficient-VQGAN: Towards High-Resolution Image Generation with Efficient Vision Transformers
2023.tldr: Makes two-stage VQ image generation efficient at high resolution: local-window Transformer blocks replace global attention for vector quantization, and multi-grained attention is paired with autoencoding training and autoregressive inference. Improves both fidelity and speed on FFHQ and ImageNet.

2024.title: Relative Preference Optimization: Enhancing LLM Alignment through Contrasting Responses across Identical and Diverse Prompts
2024.tldr: DPO only compares two responses to the same prompt. RPO also contrasts responses across semantically related prompts, weighting each pair by prompt similarity, so it can learn from both paired and unpaired preference data. Outperforms DPO, IPO, and KTO on Anthropic-HH, OpenAI Summarization, and AlpacaEval 2.0.

2024.title: Self-Augmented Preference Optimization: Off-Policy Paradigms for Language Model Alignment
2024.tldr: Preference alignment without paired preference data or an external reward model. SAPO builds its own negatives by regenerating segments of chosen responses, using an EMA model and a replay buffer to keep training pairs fresh as the policy improves. Matches or exceeds DPO, ORPO, and SPIN on the Open LLM Leaderboard, IFEval, MT-Bench, and AlpacaEval 2.0.

2024.title: Diffusion-RPO: Aligning Diffusion Models through Relative Preference Optimization
2024.tldr: Extends RPO to text-to-image diffusion models, contrasting images generated from identical and semantically related prompts with step-wise weighting. Also introduces a style-alignment evaluation task, and outperforms Diffusion-DPO and SFT on Stable Diffusion 1.5 and XL.

2025.title: Segmenting Text and Learning Their Rewards for Improved RLHF in Language Model
2025.tldr: A single reward per response is too sparse for RLHF, and a single token is too small to carry meaning. We split responses into semantically complete segments using the SFT model's entropy, learn segment-level rewards from ordinary sequence-level preferences, and stabilize PPO with location-aware reward normalization and within-segment reward interpolation. Outperforms sequence-, sentence-, and token-level reward variants on AlpacaEval 2.0, Arena-Hard, and MT-Bench.

2025.title: KODCODE: A Diverse, Challenging, and Verifiable Synthetic Dataset for Coding
awards: 🏆 Best Paper Award at DataWorld @ ICML 2025
2025.tldr: A synthetic coding dataset of 447K question–solution–test triplets from 12 sources. Each solution is verified by executing its unit tests, and hard problems get extra attempts so they are not filtered out. Models fine-tuned on KodCode reach state-of-the-art results on HumanEval(+), MBPP(+), BigCodeBench, and LiveCodeBench, and the data also supports RL with verifiable rewards.

2026.title: Context-Grounded Data Curation and Gate-First RL Reward Design for SQL Autocomplete
2026.tldr: Autocomplete models trained on editing logs learn to guess, because the logged completion often depends on information not yet visible at the cursor. We trim each SFT target to its longest context-inferable prefix, keep empty targets as silence labels, and in RL place deterministic abstention and grounding gates before a graded LLM-judge reward, which avoids the silence collapse of a judge-only reward. The deployed 4B dense model raised live acceptance from 17.8% to 26.35% over the previous 30B-A3B MoE while cutting median latency by 71%.

2026.title: Mitigating Exploration Bias in RL for Multi-Instruction Following
2026.tldr: When a prompt contains several instructions and the reward counts how many are satisfied, RL keeps improving the easy instructions while the hard ones barely move. We propose two metrics that measure this exploration bias, then reduce it in two stages: Behavioral Bootstrapping, a short rejection-sampling fine-tuning that activates hard instructions before RL, and Scarcity-Aware Rewards, which weight each instruction by how rarely it is satisfied. Beats the cumulative-reward baseline by up to 9.2 points on IFBench.

2026.title: ContextCheck: Sentence-Level Faithfulness Verification with Context-Aware Disambiguation
2026.tldr: Checks each generated sentence against the source document while reading the preceding sentences to resolve pronouns, references, and ellipsis, removing the separate decontextualization step of prior pipelines. Earlier context is used only to disambiguate; evidence comes only from the source. Gains 10+ Macro-F1 points on three new context-dependent benchmarks and matches or beats 8B-scale verifiers on 14 standard single-sentence datasets.

experience.description: Now building training datasets for terminal and SWE agents and working on long-horizon RL training. Earlier, worked on SQL autocomplete: post-trained a 4B dense fill-in-the-middle model that replaced a 30B-A3B MoE in production, with context-grounded SFT data and a gate-first RL reward that teaches the model when to suggest and when to stay silent (NeurIPS'26 Workshop).
Built ContextCheck, a sentence-level faithfulness verifier that reads the preceding context to resolve references while drawing evidence only from the source document (ACL Findings'26).

Developed Segment-PPO, which learns rewards for semantically complete text segments to give PPO denser feedback (TMLR'25), and contributed to KodCode, a verifiable synthetic coding dataset for SFT and RL (ACL Findings'25; Best Paper at DataWorld @ ICML'25).
Worked on continuous and discrete diffusion models: DiffGAR for restoring artifacts in generated images (CSAI'22) and Efficient-VQGAN for high-resolution image generation (ICCV'23).
Developed TransEditor, a Transformer-based dual-space GAN for controllable facial editing (CVPR'22), and an audio-driven talking-face generation system.
